title: Rock in Rio 2026 Draws Crowds with Diverse Shows
seoTitle: Rock in Rio 2026: Diverse Shows, International & National.
subtitle: The festival features international and national artists on distinct stages
excerpt: Rock in Rio 2026 continues to surprise with a diverse musical menu, from rock and metal to pop and electronic, keeping the audience ecstatic.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Rock in Rio 2026 upholds its tradition of bringing together artists from various genres, creating a musical mosaic that attracts crowds of all ages. The lineup, divided into Sunset and Mundo stages, features shows ranging from classic rock to EDM, ensuring every audience member finds something to enjoy.

Diversity of Genres on the Sunset Stage

The Sunset stage hosted performances spanning rock to metal, including MPB, bossa nova, and jazz. Foo Fighters closed Friday with a solid performance, while Péricles brought a mix of samba and soul. The British band Hot Milk also performed but faced a more modest audience.

Calvin Harris Dominates the Mundo Stage with a Rave

As a headliner, Calvin Harris led a massive rave on the Mundo stage, blending pop and electronic music. The DJ kept the crowd energized until the end, even in the rain. His performance featured hits like “One Kiss” with Dua Lipa and “This Is What You Came For” with Rihanna, as well as tributes to Brazilian funk.

Demi Lovato and Other Names on the Mundo Stage

On Saturday night (12), Demi Lovato performed on the Mundo stage, scheduled to start at 9:20 PM. The event's broadcast was offered by Multishow and Canal Bis, with 4K options for Globoplay Premium subscribers. TV Globo also aired glimpses of the festival during its evening programming.

Audience Reaction and Technical Challenges

While most shows were well-received, some faced technical challenges. Luísa Sonza's performance had sound problems, while Nelly's lacked well-planned transitions. In contrast, Jon Batiste's show was described as a spiritual practice that united different musical styles.

Conclusion on Cultural Impact

Rock in Rio 2026 reaffirms its role as a stage for cultural convergence, featuring international and national artists in performances that celebrate Brazilian and global musical diversity.

With information from G1, Folha de S.Paulo, Omelete.
